message.content:
Lions (family Felidae) and zebras (family Equidae) both belong to the super‑order **Laurasiatheria**.  
Their most recent common ancestor was therefore a small, insectivorous mammal that lived in the **Paleocene epoch** (about 66–56 million years ago). This ancestor was a member of the early Laurasiatherian radiation that eventually gave rise to the diverse groups of carnivores, odd‑toed ungulates, hoofed mammals, bats, and whales.
